newsitem.title: GERMANY: Asiana targets growing Korea-Europe mkt.
newsitem.headline: Asiana targets growing Korea-Europe mkt.

text.p: South Korean carrier Asiana Airlines said it would add flights to Europe this year and in 1998 and 1999 to try and capture a substantial share of the growing passenger and cargo market.
The private airline launched non-stop flights to Germany, Belgium and Austria at the end of May and would add Britain, France and Poland within the next two years, a company statement said.
The passenger market between Korea and Europe grew 19.7 percent to 961,000 travellers in 1996 and was expected to rise to 1.1 million this year, it added.
Asiana expected the number of flights from Korea to Europe to grow 20 percent annually due to the strong growth of the Korean economy.
"European demand for Korea should increase five percent per annum through the growing number of frequent flyers," the statement added.
In Germany, Asiana started twice-weekly non-stop flights between Seoul and Frankfurt with a Boeing 747 combi aircraft with 271 seats and 35 tonnes of airfreight capacity on May 29.
The airline, which will compete with Deutsche Lufthansa AG and Korean Air Lines as the third nonstop carrier, said it was targeting a 69 percent passenger seat load factor this year.

"Asiana will not try to capture the market through price but through a high quality and excellent service. Prices have been matched to those of competitors in the introductory phase," the statement said.
Target groups were Korean and Japanese residents in Germany, business travellers and tourists visiting countries such as China or Australia, it said.
Asiana said it had also split a two-year-old flight to Vienna and Brussels into separate twice-weekly Boeing 767 and Boeing 747 Combi flights respectively.
A twice-weekly B767 service had also been started to Istanbul.

Asiana said it planned to start flights to Warsaw later this year, to London in 1998 and to Paris in 1999 as its other major new European destinations. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
